newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Intel busy ahead of earnings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Intel busy ahead of earnings.

text.p: Options investors were active in semiconductor giant Intel Corp ahead of its quarterly profit announcement but had ittle reaction to some of the early first quarter company earnings.
Intel was scheduled to report after the close of trading on Monday. By late afternoon, more than 60,000 Intel options had traded at the American Stock Exchange.
"The place is such a zoo," Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners, said of the Intel trading post.
Traders said there did not appear to be a one-way bias to the trading, with call and put sellers and buyers active.
Intel shares were up 3-1/4 to 133-5/8 in afternoon trading after falling 6-3/4 last Friday. Volume Monday was about 18.3 million shares.

According to First Call, analysts' consensus estimates for Intel's first quarter profit was $2.07 a share, but stock traders said a "whisper number" of $2.15 to $2.20 was making its way through Wall Street.
Among Intel options, the April 135 call and 130 put were the most active, with volume of 7,710 and 7,330, respectively.
In the April series, the 130 and 140 calls also were very active, as were the 125 and 135 puts.
Trading was fairly heavy in the May series as well, led by the 135 and 140 calls, which traded 2,870 and 2,790 contracts, respectively.
After peaking at 164-3/4 on a closing basis on February 4, Intel shares fell to a 130-1/2 close on March 21 before rebounding.
The stock then rallied to close at 146-5/8 about a week ago and began another decline that ended at Friday's 130-1/2 close.
Trading in Intel options was frenzied, but action in options on a couple of stocks that reported solid earnings Monday was slim, dealers said.
General Motors Corp earlier reported first quarter operating profits of $2.30 a share, up from $0.93 a share in the first quarter of 1996.
Also, Coca-Cola Co reported first quarter earnings of $0.40 a share, which beat Wall Street estimates by $0.02 a share. The company earned $0.28 in the first quarter of last year.
But neither GM nor Coca-Cola options were especially busy, even as the shares firmed.
GM added 5/8 to 53-5/8 and Coca-Cola gained 1-7/8 to 55-5/8.
"There been a lot trading, but nothing out of the ordinary," one trader in Coca-Cola options said. He added that volatilities remained firm.
The Coca-Cola May 55 put traded more than 3,900 contracts, making it most active in the group. The May 55 call traded about 3000 and the May 60 call traded 1,215.
The busiest GM option was the April 55 call with 450.
